tagline: Analog Roots First, Digital Wings Later — 100% Screen-Free Books for Ages 0–7
manifestoTitle: Before They Fly, Anchor Their Roots
mission: Human Edge Press is an independent Austin, Texas publisher dedicated to early childhood screen-free development—publishing neuroscience-backed high-contrast baby board books, tactile STEAM alphabet books, character virtue hardcovers, Pre-K workbooks, and Socratic parent guides that build the human capacities no algorithm can replace.
location: 100 Innovation Way, Suite 400, Austin, TX 78701, United States

coreBeliefs.title: 1. Real Pages Build Real Focus
coreBeliefs.summary: During ages 0–7, young children experience a documented 'transfer deficit' with 2D screens—struggling to transfer lessons from glass to real life—while physical page-turning builds spatial memory and sustained executive attention.

coreBeliefs.title: 2. A Parent's Voice Beats Any Algorithm
coreBeliefs.summary: Back-and-forth eye contact, pointing, expression-copying, and unhurried conversation ('serve and return') wire language and emotional security far deeper than passive audio buttons or auto-playing apps.

coreBeliefs.title: 3. Big Ideas Belong in Little Hands
coreBeliefs.summary: Science, simple tools, engineering balance, art, and number sense begin with wooden blocks, kitchen-table experiments, and outdoor observation—not coding tablets for toddlers.

coreBeliefs.title: 4. Character & Virtue Are the True Human Edge
coreBeliefs.summary: As commodity AI automates routine output, distinctly human virtues—kindness, bravery, patience, honesty, empathy, focus, persistence, curiosity, creativity, gratitude, helpfulness, and listening—become a child's lifelong advantage.

coreBeliefs.title: 5. Strategic Timing From Infancy to Young Adulthood
coreBeliefs.concept: Protecting Cortical Stamina & Developing The Human Veto
coreBeliefs.summary: Human Edge Press is pro-childhood, not anti-technology: anchor deep focus, tactile mastery, and independent judgment first so teens and young adults command technology with 'The Human Veto' rather than being hijacked by variable dopamine loops.
